observations: Manual sewing machine mounted on a wooden table with a metal treadle stand.
The brand 'MERCURY' is visible on the machine head in photo 0 and 1.
The brand 'SUMOPREMIUM' is visible on the treadle foot plate in photo 1 and 2.
Significant paint chipping and wear are visible on the top right of the machine head in all photos.
The drive belt connecting the handwheel to the treadle wheel is missing in photo 3.
The wooden table surface shows some scuffing and wear.
The machine appears to be a zig-zag capable model based on the dials on the front.

claims.evidence: Photo 0 shows significant paint loss on the head; photo 3 shows the drive belt is missing.

risks.risk: The machine may be seized or have internal mechanical timing issues.
risks.proof: A video showing the handwheel being turned and the needle bar moving smoothly through a full cycle.

risks.risk: Missing drive belt prevents immediate use.
risks.proof: A photo of the machine with a belt installed.

risks.risk: Missing essential accessories like bobbins, bobbin case, or specific presser feet.
risks.proof: A photo of all included accessories and the bobbin area.

proof_requests: Video of the machine's handwheel being turned to demonstrate the needle and feed dogs moving.
Photo of the bobbin case and any included accessories.
Close-up photo of the underside of the machine head to check for rust.
response.reason: The item is clearly identified as a Mercury sewing machine on a Sumopremium stand. While the seller's claim of perfect condition is false due to visible cosmetic damage and a missing belt, it can be priced at its worst-case value as a non-functional unit requiring parts and repair.
